about.title: Livingston Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Livingston is a small, tight-knit Merced County community, but its roads still see real traffic risk. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 35 injury collisions and 43 injured people, with three lives lost. Local data shows crashes cluster on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., often along Hammatt Avenue, Walnut Avenue, F Street, and Main Street — corridors that carry heavy commuter and agricultural traffic. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the choices you make in the first days matter: what you say to an insurance adjuster, whether photos and witness contact information get preserved, and how quickly medical care is documented. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Livingston residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, without any upfront cost or obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road or Merced County vehicle — is involved. Waiting too long can close the door on your claim entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're found partly at fault — your share is simply subtracted from any award. An attorney can help make sure fault percentages assigned by an insurer are fair and supported by evidence.

items.title: No Cap Means Insurers Push Back Harder
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, which is exactly why insurance companies often try to get a recorded statement early, before you've spoken with anyone else. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say — and what to avoid saying — before that call happens.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to look for ways to shift fault or minimize your claim. An independent attorney can advise you on how to respond, or whether to respond at all.

items.question: What if my crash happened on a city street like F Street or Main Street in Livingston?
items.answer: Local roads are usually maintained by the city or Merced County, and if road conditions or a government vehicle contributed to the crash, special short deadlines — sometimes just six months — can apply. It's important to have someone look at the circumstances of your crash quickly so no filing deadline is missed.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can ask questions and get a sense of your options before deciding how to move forward.
